note: flags from an independent visual reviewer who looked at the compare images

flags.problem: Grey concrete wall reads correctly in tone, but the 1:1 crop has horizontal streak banding about every 4-8 px and speckled noise that look like scanline artifacts rather than concrete pores. Original has only a few dark grid lines.
flags.fix: Remove the periodic horizontal component from the LAB high-frequency layer (grain metric shows a 4 px period), reduce HF noise amplitude, and re-check the 1:1 crop for streaks.

flags.problem: Fog gradient matches the original in full-height layout and tone, but the 1:1 centre crop shows a hard horizontal cutoff: a purple block ends abruptly about 64 px down and the area below is magenta (transparent). That conflicts with the full-height gradient in the fit view. It may be a compare-tool crop artifact or a real alpha bug.
flags.fix: Re-render the compare from the raw RGBA at 1:1 and check alpha row by row across the full height. If alpha really drops out mid-height, fix the soft-alpha reconstruction so it fades smoothly to the bottom. Otherwise fix the compare crop and mark good.
